[prelude] I've never had good experiences with LG devices and had a stupidly high failure rate. It's probably bad luck, but my usual stance against LG can be summed up as:
Gamers Nexus investigation claim LG TVs capture audio in standby
Settled a Texas lawsuit over collecting viewing data without consent
Undeletable Copilot app pushed to TVs
Monitors silently installed an app via Windows Update that pushed McAfee ads
Home solar batteries recalled for fire risk (LG Energy Solutions)
Ordered to pay A$160,000 for misleading two customers about faulty-TV rights, after ACCC action
Federal Court declared its phone manuals misrepresented consumers' warranty rights
Offered up to A$3.1 million in rebates after air conditioners fell short of their energy ratings
ACCC undertaking over fridges marketed with incorrect energy use claims
Claimed that washing machines were water-rated before they'd been certified
LG NZ's country manager and two staff pleaded guilty after evidence requested by the regulator was deleted
Fined US$400 million for LCD price-fixing
2020 gas leak at an Indian chemical plant killed 12 people and left 585 sick (LG Chem, LG Polymers India)
Denied a hack until the government confirmed it (LG Uplus)
Fridge compressor failures led to a US settlement covering ~1.55 million owners
They're a massive company with many branches and arms, but my god they're bad.
[Ebisu] Same here! I bought an LG Blu-ray home theatre around 15 years ago, and it failed after just 13 months. Later, I needed a microwave and LG had the best deal, but I was hesitant because of my previous experience. I bought it anyway, and after just 4 months, the paint started peeling off the top. The Good Guys said it was cosmetic damage and wouldn’t do anything about it. Then, at 10 months, it stopped heating altogether, so I got a refund. Never buying LG again. Life’s no good with LG.
[BewareOfThe Dog] One of the best notebooks I owned was the LG LM50-3. It was such a good unit, till I dropped it. My MacBook is great, but I prefer Windows OS.
